title: Used up a little at a time
odia:
ଗୁଡ ଚାଖୁ ଚାଖୁ ଯାଏ
ତେଲ ମାଖୁ ମାଖୁ ଯାଏ।
literal_meaning: Jaggery goes as you keep tasting it; oil goes as you keep applying it.
meaning_odia: ବାରମ୍ବାର ଅଳ୍ପ ଅଳ୍ପ ଚାଖିଲେ ଗୁଡ ସରେ, ଅଳ୍ପ ଅଳ୍ପ ମାଖିଲେ ତେଲ ସରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଛୋଟ ଛୋଟ ବ୍ୟବହାରର ମୋଟ ପରିମାଣକୁ ଧ୍ୟାନ ଦେବାର କଥା ଏଠାରେ ଅଛି—ଥରକୁ ଅଳ୍ପ ଲାଗିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ବାରମ୍ବାର ହେଲେ ଭଣ୍ଡାର କମିଯାଏ।
explanation: Each taste or application may seem small, but repetition draws down the supply. Our editorial reading connects the two everyday actions as an image of gradual depletion. The verse makes the accumulating effect noticeable through its repeated verbs.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Small withdrawals from a shared supply seem negligible until the container is nearly empty. Someone quotes the saying to explain how repeated little uses add up.
cultural_context: ଚାଖୁ ଚାଖୁ and ମାଖୁ ମାଖୁ echo each other in sound and rhythm. One line tastes, the other applies, but both end with ଯାଏ: the substance is going. The paired structure turns repetition itself into the explanation.

english_summary: Repeated small uses gradually consume a supply.
